fixes.explanation: Good guess, because shepherding does come up in this psalm. But that comes at the very end, when David asks the LORD to "shepherd them and carry them forever." (Psalm 28:9) In verse 1, David says that if the LORD stays silent, he'll be like those descending to the Pit. I'd say shepherding asked for at the end is a long way from the Pit at the start.
Riches? No wish list for the bank here. David lifts his hands toward the LORD's holy sanctuary and calls to Him for help, and he asks to be heard. (Psalm 28:2) Not one coin gets mentioned.

It's actually true, friend. Psalm 28:5 says, "Since they show no regard for the works of the LORD or what His hands have done, He will tear them down and never rebuild them." The verse gives the reason and the result together.
That's it, baker. David says, "my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped." (Psalm 28:7) The LORD is his strength and his shield, and his heart puts its trust in Him. That's the right place for it.

No hiding mentioned here, friend. David says, "my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped." (Psalm 28:7) He goes on to say, "Therefore my heart rejoices…" The verse says his heart trusts and rejoices, not that it hides.

That's the closer, baker! David prays, "Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever." (Psalm 28:9) Save, bless, shepherd, carry, and then he says FOREVER. He doesn't ask for a little carrying, friend, he asks for it forever.
